en.title: Minimum Operations to Run Tasks in Parallel
en.description:
In one operation, choose an unfinished task and run it for x seconds while every other task runs for y seconds, where y<x; a task exits once its accumulated run time reaches its required time. Find the minimum number of operations needed to finish all tasks. The original snapshot restores y<x.

The input/output protocol was compiled independently by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains n x y, and the second line contains n execution times; 1≤n≤100000, 1≤time≤10⁹, 1≤y<x≤10⁹.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 3; 1; 6. All examples have been verified by independent small-scale enumeration or state search.
hints: Binary search on the number of operations t; first give every task a base amount of ty, then divide each task's remaining need by x−y, rounding up, to get how many extra times it must be the main task. t is feasible if the sum does not exceed t.
